symbols.name: SNAPSHOT_REL

symbols.name: MAX_HORIZON_DAYS
symbols.note: Maximum allowed acceptance horizon in days (90).

symbols.name: ISLAND_CLASSES
symbols.note: Reach classes treated as islands: island, orphan.

symbols.name: UNKNOWN_CLASSES
symbols.note: Reach classes treated as unknown: unknown.

symbols.name: SHIM_CLASSES

symbols.name: UNREACHED_CLASSES

claims.text: The artifact was not wrong when it was written; it went stale immediately and nobody could tell.
claims.why: Historical narrative; not checkable against code.

claims.text: This module compares the CURRENT generated state against a COMMITTED snapshot (docs/architecture-state.json) and fails when they disagree.
claims.why: The comparison logic is not in this chunk; SNAPSHOT_REL is defined but used elsewhere.

claims.text: The snapshot is deliberately small, sorted and free of timestamps.
claims.why: Snapshot format not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: This module DERIVES NOTHING ITSELF. Islands come from reach.analyse; switches come from switches.analyse; both are the same reports the page renders, computed once and passed in.
claims.why: The functions that use reach/switches are not in this chunk.

claims.text: UNREACHED = every reach class that means 'no entry point gets here', UNREACHED_CLASSES, split across THREE lists
claims.why: UNREACHED_CLASSES is defined as ISLAND_CLASSES + UNKNOWN_CLASSES + SHIM_CLASSES, and the three lists are defined separately.

claims.text: islands: reach's island + orphan. Those two are merged because the remedy really is identical
claims.why: ISLAND_CLASSES = ('island', 'orphan') on line 98.

claims.text: unknown: reach could not tell.
claims.why: UNKNOWN_CLASSES = ('unknown',) on line 103.

claims.text: shims: a re-export nothing reaches.
claims.why: SHIM_CLASSES = ('shim',) on line 106.

claims.text: These three used to be one list containing only the first, and the other two were dropped on the floor
claims.why: Historical statement; no code in this chunk to verify.

claims.text: Every unreached module is now counted, in exactly one of the three lists, and counts['unreached'] is their total
claims.why: The counting logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: the three lists together are a function of reach's classification and can only drift from it if UNREACHED_CLASSES stops covering a class reach can emit.
claims.why: The classification logic is in reach module; not in this chunk.

claims.text: DARK = switches' dark verdict, MINUS the ones it classifies secret, MINUS the ones documented BY THIS FILE'S RULE
claims.why: The dark switch computation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Darkness itself -- off by default, no fallback, in a boolean position -- is decided in exactly one place, switches
claims.why: The switches module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The secret carve-out is a judgement call worth arguing with
claims.why: No code in this chunk.

claims.text: Reachability is the transitive closure of the import graph from DISCOVERED entry points (console scripts, __main__.py, __main__ guards, CLI dispatch branches, HTTP routes, poll loops).
claims.why: Reachability logic is in reach module; not in this chunk.

claims.text: A module reached only by its own test is STILL AN ISLAND here, and it is reported as one -- but under its own kind, TEST_ONLY, which does not block.
claims.why: TEST_ONLY is not defined in this chunk; logic elsewhere.

claims.text: An environment variable that (a) is consumed as a BOOLEAN GATE, (b) defaults OFF with no fallback, and (c) is not documented.
claims.why: The dark switch detection logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: (a) and (b) are switches's judgement, verbatim.
claims.why: Switches module not in this chunk.

claims.text: (c) is this file's, and it is stricter than 'the token appears somewhere'
claims.why: The documentation detection logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A switch counts as documented when ... it appears in a form an operator would actually type ... and beside at least MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS characters of other prose
claims.why: The parsing logic is not in this chunk; MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS is defined but not used here.

claims.text: Code fences are excluded because a fenced sample is where a name most often appears without being explained
claims.why: The fence exclusion logic is not in this chunk; _FENCE_RE is defined but not used here.

claims.text: GENERATED_DOCS is excluded because daedalus map renders that file INTO the artifact this gate guards
claims.why: GENERATED_DOCS is defined but its usage is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This is deliberately not 'one designated inventory file with a description'
claims.why: Design rationale; no code in this chunk.

claims.text: TIER 1 -- TEMPORARY, DATED, SELF-RESURFACING (acceptances in the snapshot)
claims.why: Acceptance mechanics are not in this chunk.

claims.text: EXPLICIT AND GREPPABLE -- grep -n 'island:' docs/architecture-state.json lists every island anyone is currently looking away from.
claims.why: Snapshot format not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: RECORDS WHY AND WHEN -- why under MIN_WHY_CHARS characters is rejected, and both dates are required.
claims.why: MIN_WHY_CHARS is defined but the validation logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: BOUND TO THE CALENDAR, NOT ONLY TO ITSELF. until is capped at MAX_HORIZON_DAYS past since AND since may not be in the future.
claims.why: MAX_HORIZON_DAYS is defined but the date validation logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The cap alone was not enough: {"since": "2999-01-01", "until": "2999-03-01"} is a 59-day horizon and parsed clean, so it suppressed forever
claims.why: The parsing logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Past until the acceptance stops suppressing and the underlying item comes back with the acceptance's own prose attached
claims.why: The expiration logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: An accepted item is NEVER written into the baseline (see write_snapshot).
claims.why: write_snapshot is not in this chunk.

claims.text: An acceptance that matches nothing is a STALE ACCEPTANCE and blocks.
claims.why: The stale acceptance check is not in this chunk.

claims.text: TIER 2 -- PERMANENT, BY REVIEWED DIFF (--refresh). Deleting the acceptance and re-baselining moves the item into islands/dark_switches and bumps counts.
claims.why: The refresh logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Every mechanical list is covered by a DIGEST_KEY over the canonical bytes, so hand-editing islands or dark_switches to pre-seed a finding into the baseline is an INVALID SNAPSHOT rather than a silent pass.
claims.why: DIGEST_KEY is not defined in this chunk; digest logic elsewhere.

claims.text: The lists are additionally required to be internally coherent (islands, unknown and shims are subsets of modules; test_only is a subset of their union) and grounded in reality (dark_switches must name variables the code still reads).
claims.why: The validation logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: WHAT THAT SENTENCE IS ALLOWED TO CLAIM is exactly this: every verb in this subsystem that READS a snapshot re-derives the digest first and refuses a mismatch.
claims.why: The digest verification logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: check reports INVALID SNAPSHOT.
claims.why: The check function is not in this chunk.

claims.text: render.accept -- which inherits the mechanical lists verbatim in order not to bank unrelated drift -- refuses to inherit them at all unless the digest it is inheriting verifies
claims.why: render module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: refresh does not need the check: it rescans and overwrites every mechanical list from the tree.
claims.why: The refresh function is not in this chunk.

claims.text: It does not stop somebody who runs Python to re-compute the digest, and it is not meant to
claims.why: No code in this chunk.

claims.text: DAEDALUS_IGNORE and .daedalusignore narrow the structural index.
claims.why: The ignore configuration logic is not in this chunk; constants are defined but not used here.

claims.text: Since the gate now reads the tree through reach, which walks the filesystem itself, they cannot narrow what the gate sees
claims.why: The reach module is not in this chunk.

claims.text: the configuration is recorded in the snapshot and compared on every run anyway
claims.why: Snapshot recording logic not in this chunk.

claims.text: A missing snapshot is NOT a pass. Both entry points refuse it: daedalus map --check exits non-zero, and python -m daedalus.mapping.drift does too.
claims.why: The entry point logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Writing a baseline is an explicit named action (--init, --refresh, or a plain daedalus map)
claims.why: The CLI logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: This is a CI GATE, NOT A PRE-COMMIT HOOK.
claims.why: No code in this chunk.

claims.text: A full run parses every Python file in the tree twice (reachability and switches) and takes seconds, not milliseconds.
claims.why: Performance claim; no code in this chunk.

claims.text: Wired into pre-commit it would be bypassed with --no-verify within a week
claims.why: Speculative claim; no code in this chunk.

claims.text: 2: single-engine state. Adds test_only/unparsable/ignore/digest and re-derives islands and dark switches from reach/switches, so a schema-1 baseline cannot be compared against a schema-2 run
claims.why: Schema history comment; no code in this chunk to verify.

claims.text: 3: the unreached half stops being one list. unknown and shims join islands as first-class lists with their own counts and their own gate kinds, counts['unreached'] is their total, and index_extra_edges records where the two engines disagree about the import graph.
claims.why: Schema description; no code in this chunk to verify the actual lists and counts.

claims.text: Within 3, additively: repo_state records WHICH TREE was scanned and is covered by the digest.
claims.why: No code in this chunk for repo_state.

claims.text: Not a version bump, because the lists still mean what they meant -- a schema-3 baseline without it simply cannot answer the freshness question, which snapshot_freshness reports as 'not fresh' rather than pretending otherwise.
claims.why: snapshot_freshness is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The teeth. An acceptance may not be written further out than this, so no acceptance can outlive a release cycle without a human retyping the reason.
claims.why: The enforcement logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: wip is not a reason. Short enough to be typeable, long enough to be a sentence.
claims.why: The validation logic using MIN_WHY_CHARS is not in this chunk.

claims.text: orphan is reach's strictly-worse island (imports nothing, imported by nothing, untested); the remedy is the same, so the gate does not split them.
claims.why: Reach's classification details are not in this chunk.

claims.text: unknown and shim are ALSO 'no entry point gets here' -- reach says so itself -- but they are not islands and must not be flattened into them
claims.why: Reach's classification details are not in this chunk.

claims.text: What may never happen again is a reach class that means unreached and appears in none of them.
claims.why: This is a policy statement; enforcement is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Everything reach can emit that is NOT unreached. Together with UNREACHED_CLASSES this must cover reach.CLASSES exactly; the property is asserted in the tests, because a new reach class silently landing outside both sets is precisely how two classes got dropped the first time.
claims.why: The test assertion is not in this chunk; reach.CLASSES is not defined here.

claims.text: Files this artifact GENERATES AGAINST. Counting a mention here would let the page document away its own findings.
claims.why: The usage of GENERATED_DOCS is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Prose that has to sit beside the name before a mention counts as an explanation. Roughly 'five words': long enough that a bare token and a two-word label both fail, short enough that a real one-line entry passes.
claims.why: The threshold logic is not in this chunk.
